title: Example 111: a PaymentVoided event added to the sealed PaymentEvent family without its @JsonSubTypes entry, caught by the wire types of the boundary contract (B12)
description: The first example of the wire types in a boundary contract: jvmcontract reads the Jackson annotations and the PermittedSubclasses attribute of the Box Office contracts module and writes the JSON shape of each message family into src/contract/boundaries.contract. The patch adds a PaymentVoided record to the sealed PaymentEvent interface, publishes it in payment-service and handles it in ticketing-service, without adding it to @JsonSubTypes. The change is intended, so the runner regenerates the contract and reports as the violation the new ! line: PaymentVoided is a permitted subtype that @JsonSubTypes does not list, written under the type id PaymentEvent$PaymentVoided which a reader rejects (checked against Jackson 3.1). The runner compiles the patched contracts module with Gradle offline and runs jvmcontract update then verify; the module's own tests (MessageCodecTest) run first and pass, since they round-trip only the events they name.
expected: build.py 111 exits 0: verdict violation, 1 new problem, matches expected
